releases.body:
## What's in v0.3.5

Robustness hardening for eval identity, frontmatter parsing, and the managed-skill installer.

### Per-item eval identity (H2)
`skill_eval` now aggregates run outcomes by **eval-set index** instead of query text, so duplicate queries keep their own labels, counts, and per-item errors, and results come back in eval-set order. Scoring, denominator, cancellation, and error behavior are unchanged. No public tool-signature change.

### Positional train/test split (H3)
`skill_optimize_loop` slices the holdout **positionally** against `[...trainSet, ...testSet]`. A query duplicated across the train/test boundary is no longer merged by text, so the holdout score is not contaminated.

### Bounded block scalars in frontmatter (H5)
`skill_parse` reads the accepted block-scalar subset — indicator `|`/`>`, chomping `+`/`-`, explicit indent `1-9` in either order — with literal breaks/indent/trailing spaces, folded adjacent/blank/more-indented handling, and chomping that mirrors the YAML reference (`-` strip, default clip, `+` keep). CRLF is normalized in the scalar value only; `fullContent` bytes are untouched. This is a **bounded** reader for the accepted grammar, not a general YAML parser.

### Upgrade-safe skill ownership (H4)
The bundled-skill installer records only the regular files it copies (relative path + sha256) in an internal ownership manifest. On upgrade it removes only a **recorded, on-disk-unchanged, regular** file that the new bundle no longer ships and whose path stays inside the managed directory. It lstats the managed root and every ancestor and refuses to prune through any symlink. `SKILL.md`, `SKILL.md.user-backup`, the version marker, and the manifest are reserved and are never tracked or pruned (compared case-insensitively for the reserved root names). Legacy installs without a manifest prune nothing; malformed manifests (including an array `files` shape) prune nothing. The manifest is written **before** the version marker, so a metadata-write failure holds the old version and reports via `onError` (best-effort ordering, not an atomic two-file transaction). No blanket recursive wipe, no new dependency.

## Credit

Thanks to @sogeisetsu for the evaluation, parsing, and installer improvement proposals in [#42](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/42), adapted in [#49](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/49).

Automated release for opencode-skill-creator v0.3.4.

## What's changed

OpenCode V1 now closes each plugin instance's review servers on unload, releasing their ports without affecting other instances. Repeated disposal is safe; existing V2 cleanup is unchanged.

## Credit

Thanks to @sogeisetsu for the V1 unload-cleanup proposal in [#41](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/41), adapted in [#48](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/48).

Automated release for `opencode-skill-creator` v0.3.3.

## What's changed
`skill_validate` now normalizes CRLF→LF once at read time, so `SKILL.md` files written by Windows checkouts (`core.autocrlf=true`) validate correctly instead of failing with `Invalid frontmatter format`. Because `skill_eval` / `skill_optimize_loop` validate before starting, this also unblocks evals on CRLF checkouts. The change is CRLF-only and read-only — no CR/BOM/trim/parser/YAML/dependency/engine changes, and `parseSkillMd` is untouched.

## Credit

Thanks to @sogeisetsu for the CRLF frontmatter fix proposed in [#40](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/40), adapted in [#47](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/47).

Automated release for `opencode-skill-creator` v0.3.2.

## What's changed
`skill_serve_review` now opens the eval review page with a **platform-specific** launcher instead of the hardcoded macOS `open`:
- macOS: `open <url>`
- Linux / other Unix: `xdg-open <url>`
- Windows: `cmd /c start "" <url>`

A new exported `browserOpenCommand(url, platform)` selects the command and arguments. `defaultOpenBrowser` uses it and also routes synchronous spawn failures through `onError`, on top of the existing asynchronous `error` listener. A missing launcher stays best-effort: the review server remains up and reports the manual URL. The interactive default (`openBrowser: true`) is unchanged; automated callers still opt out via `openBrowser: false` / `OPENCODE_SKILL_CREATOR_OPEN_BROWSER=0`.

## Credit

Thanks to @sogeisetsu for the browser-launching proposal in [#39](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/39), adapted in [#46](https://github.com/antongulin/opencode-skill-creator/pull/46).
